claims.text: What the strip looks like Sinus rhythm whose rate rises and falls w breathing, so the beat-to-beat spacing var.
claims.quote: Sinus arrhythmia: phasic variation with respiration (common and benign in young patients)

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Rate: rises slightly on inspiration and falls on expiration
claims.quote: A slight increase in rate during inspiration with a decrease in rate during expiration (respiratory sinus arrhythmia) is also normal

claims.text: Rhythm: irreg: the P-P interval var by more than 120 ms (3 sm boxes)
claims.quote: Variation in the P-P interval of more than 120 ms (3 small boxes).

claims.text: Pattern: the P-P interval lengthens and shortens in a cycle that USU follows breathing
claims.quote: The P-P interval gradually lengthens and shortens in a cyclical fashion, usually corresponding to the phases of the respiratory cycle.

claims.text: P waves: norm sinus P waves w a constant shape (⍉PACs)
claims.quote: Normal sinus P waves with a constant morphology (i.e. no evidence of premature atrial contractions).
Constant P-R interval (i.e. no evidence of Mobitz I AV block).

claims.text: QRS: each norm P = followed by its QRS (1:1)
claims.quote: An irregular QRS rhythm with a 1:1 relationship between P waves and the following QRS complexes usually indicates sinus arrhythmia with gradual acceleration and deceleration of the sinus rate (if P waves are normal).

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: reflex chgs in vagal tone w breathing — inspiration lowers vagal tone (rate rises); expiration restores it (rate falls)
claims.quote: The heart rate varies due to reflex changes in vagal tone during the different stages of the respiratory cycle. Inspiration increases the heart rate by decreasing vagal tone. With the onset of expiration, vagal tone is restored, leading to a subsequent decrease in heart rate.

claims.text: Who: a norm finding, MC in young, healthy people
claims.quote: Sinus arrhythmia is a normal physiological phenomenon, most commnonly seen in young, healthy people.
The incidence of sinus arrhythmia decreases with age

claims.text: ⍉respiratory sinus arrhythmia (⍉tied to breathing) = less common, USU in elderly pts, and more likely pathological (ex, Hdz, digoxin toxicity)
claims.quote: “Non-respiratory” sinus arrhythmia (not linked to the respiratory cycle) is less common, typically occurs in elderly patients and is more likely to be pathological (e.g. due to heart disease or digoxin toxicity).

claims.text: Don't confuse w: freq PACs, Mobitz I, type I SA exit block
claims.quote: Frequent premature atrial contractions Second-degree AV block, Mobitz I (Wenckebach phenomenon) Type I Sinoatrial Exit Block

claims.text: Sx Benign — common in young pts
claims.quote: Sinus arrhythmia: phasic variation with respiration (common and benign in young patients)

claims.text: Tx None: aSx arrhythmias w.o serious risk need ⍉tx
claims.quote: Asymptomatic arrhythmias without serious risks do not require treatment even if they worsen.

notes.issue: "QRS, ST and T: normal sinus beats" was not supported by the quote.
notes.resolution: Reworded to "QRS: each normal P is followed by its QRS (1:1)". Revised; re-checked PASS by otto-31762 at 2026-10-05.
